summary: This chest X-ray shows a large, rounded air-and-fluid-filled structure in the lower left part of the chest, situated behind and below the heart. This appearance is typical of a large hiatal (or diaphragmatic) hernia, where part of the stomach has moved up into the chest cavity through an opening in the diaphragm (the muscle that separates the chest and abdomen). This is a common condition, especially in older adults, and can sometimes cause symptoms like heartburn, difficulty swallowing, or chest discomfort, though many cases are found incidentally. In some cases, if the herniated stomach becomes twisted or obstructed, it can become an emergency. The lungs themselves appear largely clear on this image, without signs of pneumonia or significant fluid buildup. Because the image quality is limited by patient positioning, further imaging (such as a CT scan) and clinical correlation with a doctor are recommended to confirm the diagnosis and assess for any complications.
